tagline: A parkway of stone arches, run north to Bear Mountain.
intro: The parkway crosses into New York at the hamlet of Palisades and swings northwest, away from the Hudson, under stone arch overpasses and between forested buffers and planted medians. Past the Thruway at West Nyack and the last busy exit at Stony Point it enters Harriman State Park and runs on through parkland into Orange County. It ends at a traffic circle by the river, at the foot of the Bear Mountain Bridge.
The park at its north end was nearly a prison. In 1908 the state meant to move Sing Sing to Bear Mountain, until Mary Harriman offered 10,000 acres and a million dollars for a park instead.

moments.title: Harriman State Park
moments.text: The state's second largest park, with 31 lakes and more than 200 miles of volunteer-kept trail, reached from the parkway by Lake Welch Parkway and Seven Lakes Drive.

moments.title: Palisades Interstate Park Commission Visitor Center
moments.text: Just inside Orange County, a parkway service area in the center median now serves as the visitor center, with an information desk and a bookstore open to both directions.

moments.title: Bear Mountain Bridge
moments.text: When it opened in 1924 it was the longest suspension bridge in the world, for 19 months, and it still carries the Appalachian Trail across the Hudson.

practical: Commercial vehicles are prohibited on the entire parkway.
